text:
CLUSTER PIN 1 of N, build-ui skill framework. Read every pin in this cluster TOGETHER, not individually: this is one deliberation split across a grounding pass and five magi voter proposals that land separately. Later pins in the cluster carry the same marker text 'build-ui skill framework cluster'.

THIS PIN covers task 1, the grounding pass, plus the jester's proposal (the first voter home).

Grounding findings worth dreaming on: (a) the versable design canon at docs/design-language/ is already organised by exactly the UI-trait list the owner asked for, stratified elementary / composite / composition, so a new skill should INHERIT that ladder rather than invent a rival taxonomy; the canon itself warns against a sixth name for an idiom that has five. (b) The two commits held up as 'worked examples' of page renovation are actually two DIFFERENT ACTIVITIES: 8cf51c9 is a one-file vocabulary swap (+74/-76), d75f456 is a nine-file conformance batch against a binding mock (+452/-291). Treating 'renovation' as one activity mis-scopes every time. (c) A four-bucket readiness vocabulary already exists (static / ready-to-show / disabled-real / honest-bone) and is a per-segment classification, which makes it the natural companion to a per-segment renovation inventory.

Jester findings: skeleton and embryo are distinct on OPPOSITE AXES. Skeleton is full breadth / zero life (whole composition tree, real copy, nothing running, proves the layout ruling). Embryo is narrow breadth / full life (smallest vertical slice that actually runs, with real tokens, readiness states, interaction, theme). Neither means a loading skeleton; that sense is owned by 'honest bone'. Also: a planning primer should be almost entirely machine-derived, with the anti-rot rule that any sentence not regenerable by a command or a file:line citation gets deleted. Also: a builder skill that can never output 'no renovation warranted' is a rationalization engine.

PROCESS OBSERVATION worth examining: the supervisor's own voter prompt mandated at least 2 web citations while denying that voter web search. The voter caught the contradiction and flagged it instead of fabricating sources. Question for the dream: do magi voter prompts need a validation-criteria consistency check before dispatch, the way setup-check.sh already gates evidence partitioning?

CLUSTER PIN 2 of N, build-ui skill framework cluster. Read with pin-20260807203826-17 and any later pin carrying this same marker; they are one deliberation, not separate insights.

THIS PIN covers the four remaining magi voter proposals (design-system architect, product/UX lead, implementation engineer, skill-author).

THE STRONGEST FINDING, from the implementation-engineer seat, is empirical and generalizes far beyond this project: the commit held up as the worked example of a page renovation (8cf51c9) SHIPPED AND LEFT FOUR LINES OF THE OLD DIALECT BEHIND, at Settings.tsx:108,111,140,272, sitting two lines from the new dialect at :254,:286. A conversion judged by eye converts what the author looked at. This is measured proof, on the exact commit the owner named as exemplary, that style-consistency work needs GREPPABLE done-conditions rather than reviewer attention. Candidate general rule: any 'make X consistent' task ships with the command that returns zero when it is actually done, and 'I converted the file' is not that command.

SECOND: the same seat reframed the two worked commits from a SIZE distinction (small vs large) into an AXIS distinction: surface conversion is vertical (one page, many traits), trait sweep is horizontal (one trait, many pages). It verified the horizontal unit is first-class by finding two more instances (a33404d tooltips across six files, 37db191 a token collision with global blast radius). The two shapes fail differently and need different done-conditions. Worth examining whether this vertical/horizontal split generalizes to non-UI refactors.

THIRD, from the product/UX seat, a fact that invalidated a working assumption: the binding design mock contains exactly six screens and the pilot target (Settings) IS NOT ONE OF THEM. A framework assuming 'read the mock for this page' fails on run one. General lesson: check that the authority document actually covers the specific target before designing a process around consulting it.

FOURTH, a hazard class no other seat named: facts no amount of code-reading recovers. Canonical instance, from 37db191, custom spacing keys in index.css shadowed Tailwind v4's container scale, so max-w-md compiled to max-width:16px and prose collapsed to one word per line. Regenerated primers cannot contain such facts and hand-written primers rot around them, so they may need their own append-only lane, written by whoever got bitten.

FIFTH, a live disagreement to watch rather than resolve now: three seats hold that a 'skeleton' artifact is abstract and not runnable (no copy, no components), two hold that it renders with real copy and real components but zero data and zero handlers. The runnable reading is grounded in the codebase's own practice (App.tsx:406-424 boots the real shell with placeholders confined to data slots, commented 'boot and loaded chrome cannot drift'), which makes the loading state a byproduct of the structure artifact rather than a separate mandate.

SIXTH, a supervisor error worth recording: the supervisor's grounding notes flagged the pilot page's width as off-canon by applying a SIBLING APP's ladder without first measuring the target app's own conventions. A voter corrected it with citations. Cross-app canon transfer needs a measurement step, not an assumption.

CLUSTER PIN 3 of N, build-ui skill framework cluster. Read with pin-20260807203826-17 and pin-20260807204138-08. This one closes the loop: the framework was authored as a skill and then EXERCISED, and the exercise changed conclusions the deliberation had reached.

WHAT THE PILOT OVERTURNED. The skill's own rule 'measure the target app's conventions before applying any canon' immediately corrected two things the planning phase had asserted:
(a) Grounding claimed the pilot page mixed a good semantic token layer with a bad base layer. Measured, the split is 741 hits / 53 files for one dialect versus 157 / 10 for the other, and exactly 5 files speak both in one page. So the minority dialect is not 'the base layer wrongly reached into', it is a real competing dialect. Direction of the fix survived; the FRAMING did not.
(b) Grounding called the page's width off-canon by comparing it to a SIBLING APP's ladder. Measured, the target app has no convention for narrow pages at all (2xl, 3xl, 6xl, 48rem, 52rem all in use); only its four table pages agree. There was no convention to deviate from. The finding was withdrawn into a 'watch, do not chase' non-claims section.

GENERAL LESSON, worth a rule: a cross-app canon transfer needs a measurement step before it can produce a finding. Asserting that page X violates convention Y, where Y was learned in a different app, is an unmeasured claim wearing the costume of a grounded one.

SECOND, ON API DESIGN, from the kit work in the same session. Speedway encodes a card-table full-bleed pattern as four coordinated class strings across three props, repeated at 20-plus call sites. Reading them revealed the real defect is not repetition but LATENT WRONGNESS: the string hardcodes the card's padding as -mx-6, and on a compact card the right value is -mx-4, so every hand-written site is silently broken on compact cards. The fix was to have the parent publish its own padding as a CSS custom property and the child consume it, reducing adoption to one boolean. Generalizable shape: when a child must cancel a parent's spacing, the parent should PUBLISH the value rather than the child REMEMBER it. A remembered constant that mirrors another component's internal choice is a drift guard that only agrees with itself.

THIRD, A PROCESS NOTE. Every claim in this session that survived was one where a command was run and its output read. Every claim that got withdrawn was one derived from reading plus inference. The ratio was stark enough to be worth examining as evidence for the exercise-before-done rule rather than as an anecdote.
